claim_reviews.conclusion: “Pembesar suara” is a valid Malaysian Malay term for an apparatus that amplifies or reproduces sound.

claim_reviews.conclusion: The split is materially overstated for contrastive learning: Malaysian official reference material explicitly uses English “speaker” for the same electrical-device sense, while Indonesian technical usage also uses “speaker” alongside “pengeras suara.” This supports a shared synonym, although comparative frequency evidence is limited.
claim_reviews.evidence_limitation: The sources establish acceptance/usage, not directly comparable everyday frequency in Indonesia versus Malaysia.
claim_reviews.subject: National split and shared synonym

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Different-common-word” is incomplete without qualification because the canonical forms differ but overlap exists through “speaker.” No false-friend contrast is evidenced: “pengeras suara” and “pembesar suara” are transparent, semantically aligned compounds rather than misleading cross-variety lookalikes. The empty contrast is therefore preferable to inventing one.
claim_reviews.subject: Relation and false-friend contrast

rationale: Both learner answers are valid variety-associated equivalents for the loudspeaker sense, but the national split is materially overstated because “speaker” is also an accepted shared technical/everyday form in both varieties. The relation should acknowledge the shared synonym rather than presenting the forms as an unqualified national contrast. The English cue is accurate. No genuine false-friend contrast is established; the empty contrast should not be filled speculatively.
